title: Determine if Two Strings Are Close
description: Two lowercase strings are considered close if you can transform one into the other using any number of two operations: (1) swap any two existing characters, or (2) transform every occurrence of one existing character into another existing character and vice versa. Return `true` if `word1` and `word2` are close, and `false` otherwise.
constraints: word1 and word2 contain only lowercase English letters.
hints: Operation 1 lets you freely reorder characters, while Operation 2 lets you permute frequency counts among existing distinct characters.
Two strings are close iff they have the same length, the exact same set of distinct characters, and the same sorted list of character frequencies.

examples.explanation: "abc" can become "bca" using only character swaps.
Different lengths mean "a" and "aa" can never be transformed into each other.
Both use {a, b, c} with sorted frequencies [1, 2, 3].
